interface.name: polly_workspace_toplevel_manager_v1

description.summary: trusted workspace membership for foreign toplevels

interface.description: Workspace listing, creation, removal and activation use ext-workspace-v1. This restricted extension associates foreign toplevels with workspaces. Version 2 adds names, order and startup-only preference restoration. Version 3 pairs with version 3 children for bounded window-menu placement. Version 4 pairs with version 4 children for a native-caption hover grant. Version 5 pairs with version 5 children for display-local menu cascade. Version 6 pairs with version 6 children for horizontal/vertical arrangement. Version 7 adds opt-in native system-menu input requests, not menu authority. Older bindings retain their original menu semantics and have no picker.

entry.name: invalid_manager
entry.summary: workspace manager is not owned by this compositor

entry.name: invalid_workspace
entry.summary: workspace belongs to another manager binding

request.name: rename

description.summary: rename at the next workspace-manager commit

request.description: The nonempty name is at most 128 UTF-8 bytes. The workspace must belong to the supplied manager binding.

request.name: reorder

description.summary: move to a zero-based position at the next commit

request.description: Reordering does not change workspace identity, activation or membership. Positions beyond the end append; removed workspaces are ignored.

request.name: restore_begin

description.summary: stage a startup-only replacement of initial workspaces

request.description: Subsequent create_workspace requests on this manager form the ordered replacement, applied atomically at commit. Only creates may be staged. Names including their NUL terminators total at most 1 MiB. The active argument is a zero-based index in the replacement. A compositor that has mapped an application, changed workspaces or already restored preferences leaves live state untouched. No ordinary application windows are moved or destroyed. Only the trusted Shell's bootstrap toplevels can be rebound to the restored active workspace. Destroying either manager before commit discards this transaction.

event.name: restored

description.summary: startup restore result after workspace done

event.description: Result 0 retains live state; 1 applied the replacement; 2 rejected an invalid transaction. Rejection leaves the current layout unchanged.

request.name: enable_layout_picker

description.summary: opt into trusted native maximize-button hover

request.description: Only this authenticated Shell binding may enable the generic picker. Zero disables and revokes outstanding grants. One enables a single 500ms UI hover delay, not an input or placement deadline. Destroying this manager disables it. No theme identity or pointer coordinates are accepted. Check layout_picker_capabilities before enabling.

arg.name: supported
arg.summary: one supports the paired v4 grant; zero does not

arg.name: supported
arg.summary: one supports both bounded v6 arrangements; zero does not

request.name: enable_system_menu_requests

description.summary: opt into native title right-click and Alt+Space

request.description: Only the authenticated Shell may enable this paired v7 feature. One selects this exact manager binding; zero disables only its own opt-in. Replacement, disable or destruction retires armed gestures and pending requests. Without opt-in the compositor preserves the old input path. This does not register a menu surface or authorize any window command.

arg.name: supported
arg.summary: one supports paired v7 native menu requests

request.name: move_to

description.summary: move the toplevel family without activating it

request.description: The target must belong to the workspace manager binding passed to get_toplevel. The move is applied with that manager's next commit. Transient parents and descendants move together. A closed toplevel or removed workspace is ignored. Destroying this object does not cancel a previously queued move.

event.name: workspace

description.summary: current workspace membership

event.description: This event precedes the associated ext_workspace_manager_v1.done. Null means that the client no longer has a handle for the workspace. Handles are scoped to the manager binding passed to get_toplevel.

event.name: closed

description.summary: toplevel or workspace-manager binding is gone

event.description: No more events will be sent. The object is inert except for destroy.

request.name: open_menu

description.summary: bind an owned input surface to this live target

request.description: Only the trusted Shell can bind this object. The compositor associates the actual owned layer surface, target lifetime and current workspace with a fresh server epoch. Registration can precede the first menu frame; placement additionally requires that exact surface to be mapped, presented, exclusive overlay input with keyboard focus. Names and client-supplied roles are not authority. Only one menu epoch is live. Serials are nonzero, strictly increasing for this object, without wrap.

request.name: place

description.summary: request one bounded placement from a live menu

request.description: No arbitrary geometry, seat or window ID is accepted. The epoch must still name this object's menu surface and workspace. Lock, grabs, recording, non-menu exclusive focus, modal redirection, fullscreen, minimized/closed targets and unfit geometry are rejected without activation or mutation. A serial is consumed even on rejection.

event.name: result

description.summary: registration or placement admission, not presentation

event.description: Accepted open_menu returns a fresh nonzero epoch. Accepted place means the request was admitted and its configure queued, not that the client acknowledged, resized or presented. Rejection leaves layout unchanged. A lost result is an unknown transport outcome, never rollback success.

event.name: placement_state

description.summary: presented placement and currently feasible commands

event.description: Placement describes the last actually presented layout, not a request acknowledgment. Pending remains set until the matching client/frame fence completes, including recovery if a client declines exact size. Capabilities describe geometry/policy feasibility, not a menu grant. Fullscreen/maximized policy remains in foreign-toplevel state.

request.name: open_layout_picker

description.summary: consume this target's native hover grant

request.description: Same owned-surface and fresh-epoch registration as open_menu, with an additional single-use grant check against the actual native button, current frame, window lifetime, workspace and output. Placement still requires the exact mapped, presented, focused menu surface. A stale, duplicate, wrong-target or wrong-surface request is rejected without layout mutation. The grant is consumed even when registration fails.

event.name: layout_offer

description.summary: read-only actual native button and output projection

event.description: The nonzero token belongs only to this child and this hover generation. Button geometry is output-local logical coordinates; output geometry is global logical coordinates from the actual presented native frame and live output. It is not authority for placement and cannot be used to request arbitrary geometry. Moving off the button revokes an unredeemed offer; a registered picker may retain input while the pointer moves from the button into its owned surface.

request.name: cascade

description.summary: cascade current-workspace applications on the target display

request.description: The same serial, ordinary open_menu epoch and exact live input guards as place apply. A caption picker cannot grant this command. The output is the target's actually presented main output at registration and admission, not a client-supplied output or a remembered configure head. Only ordinary mapped, presented, non-minimized, non-fullscreen windows in that workspace and output participate. Transients, modal-blocked families and pending client/native frames are skipped. All eligible geometry is preflighted before any configure is sent; allocation failure, unfit size limits or no eligible windows reject without mutation. Floating sizes use normal work-area fitting, never shrinking to pack all windows. Existing scene order and focus remain. Accepted result means admitted, not all clients/frames presented. Final placement remains floating; v3 states and bits are unchanged.

request.name: arrange

description.summary: one floating arrangement of current-workspace applications

request.description: Requires arrangement_capabilities and paired v6 manager/child objects. Uses the same ordinary-menu epoch, serial, target display, eligibility, input guards and atomic preflight as cascade. A layout picker epoch never authorizes a batch command. No output, window array or arbitrary geometry is accepted. Each outer frame receives an exact integer partition of the whole work area, then its own native insets. Any client size limit or native inset that cannot fit its cell rejects the whole request before mutation, as do empty cells or no candidates. Existing scene order and focus remain. Final placement is floating, not a new persistent snap mode; v3 state and capability bits do not change. Accepted result means admitted, not all clients presented. A client may decline a suggested size; its actual final floating geometry is presented and the compositor logs a one-shot diagnostic.

event.name: system_menu_requested

description.summary: one-shot read-only native input projection

event.description: The serial is nonzero and increasing without wrap. The target is this actual tracked child, never a client-supplied ID. Anchor coordinates are output-local logical coordinates. A title gesture uses its release point's live output (including a straddling caption); keyboard input uses the presented window's main output. The output box is global. Consume once before opening the ordinary menu. No placement grant, surface registration, seat access or foreign geometry setter is added.

request.name: consume_system_menu

description.summary: retire and recheck a read-only input request

request.description: Rechecks the exact child, mapped lifetime, workspace, output, presented geometry and current input policy. Consumes even on rejection. An accepted result is not menu authority: open_menu is still required.
